checks.comparison: The one-fresh-sample integral is <=f(x)-gamma/2||grad f(x)||^2-gamma/4||grad f(y)||^2+gamma L^2/2||x-y||^2+gamma^2 L sigma^2/2. Its nonnegative gamma and gamma<=1/(2L) conditions preserve source C1 and additionally allow the trivial zero-step case. No lower-bound assumption is needed. The integrated C1 inequality has the same four coefficients and current/stale indices. Fresh-sample averaging is transported under IID and nonanticipation; the theorem does not assume the stochastic gradients themselves are independent after adaptive querying.

C1 explicitly bounds the nonnegative step by 1/(2L). Allowing gamma=0 is a proved harmless extension; the requested algorithm uses the positive source step. Differentiability and global L-smoothness remain actual hypotheses.

C2 averages k=0..K and retains coefficient 1/(2L^2(K+1)) on the stale-gradient sum and gamma*sigma^2/L on noise. It explicitly assumes a_k<=k< a_k+R, nonnegative gamma and gamma<=1/(2RL), with positive L. These match the source residual proof.
C2 uses a_k<=k and k<a_k+R, equivalent to source delays <=R-1, and gamma<=1/(2RL). R>=1 follows at k=0, so the theorem does not silently divide by a permitted zero threshold.

The raw average squared-gradient bound is 2(f(x0)-lower)/(gamma(K+1))+2gamma Lsigma^2 for arbitrary natural K. Positive gamma, gamma<=1/(2RL), global lower bound and bounded delays are explicit. This is the source telescoping core, not a public derived-budget wrapper. The actual theorem retains arbitrary K satisfying 8RL(f(x0)-lower)/eps+16sigma^2L(f(x0)-lower)/eps^2<=K and concludes the K+1 average<=eps. It uses the canonical old stepSize, whose inspected definition is the same min/noiseless formula as new tuning. Its arbitrary real lower bound can be instantiated with f(x0)-Delta; no equality to the old instance lower is required.

For measurable Phi invariant under changes to tape coordinates >=k, the actual theorem gives the product-Fubini integrability equivalence and total-expectation identity with an independent fresh kth sample. The inspected prefix_tail_independent provider yields independence of Fin k past from the tail; taking tail coordinate zero is exactly sample k. Integrability is explicit before the integral equality is used.

Under the source differentiability/smoothness, unbiased finite variance, IID samples and a_k<=k, every finite iterate is measurable and has integrable point norm squared, gradient norm squared and objective. These regularity conclusions supply later success fields without strengthening setup assumptions.

For b<=m the centered increment sum over Ico b m has integrable squared norm and expectation <=(m-b)sigma^2. Centering is at each adaptively queried gradient; IID freshness and past dependence kill cross terms. It does not assert independence of queried gradient vectors.

The kth iterate depends only on samples with indices <k, as required for applying the independent kth sample at a stale index a_k<=k. This is a derived recursion fact, not an extra oracle restriction. For b<=m and a_j<=j, x_m equals x_b minus gamma times the sum on Ico b m of the actual stale-gradient updates. The right endpoint is excluded, preserving source indexing.

The actual delay map is a_k rather than lag delta_k. Both source bounds use f(x0)-lower with an arbitrary real lower argument, enabling the approved adjusted bound. Canonical stepSize agrees with new tuning definition; the new execution adapters must transport that identity and supply masked-delay hypotheses.

Moment/integrability and descent results are conclusions from the source assumptions. Neither accuracy nor the residual estimate is an input to the source theorem. Arbitrary K remains in the raw sufficient-horizon theorem; deriving the public budget is delegated to the new convergence unit.

The actual theorem hypotheses are source differentiability/L-smoothness, finite unbiased variance, IID freshness, delay bounds and, only where needed, global lower bound and step constraints. No convexity, bounded iterates, exact known objective gap, minimizer or progress assumption was introduced.

The C1 gamma/2,gamma/4,gamma L^2/2,gamma^2 Lsigma^2/2 terms; C2 1/(2L^2(K+1)) and gamma sigma^2/L; raw rate 2Delta/(gamma(K+1))+2gamma Lsigma^2; and 8/16 sufficient horizon all match the source with the same K+1 averaging.

The analytical trajectory obeys the actual source stale-gradient update. This unit does not claim arbitrary delay sequences are realizable Ringmaster executions; the separate execution unit must establish that connection and the R-window bound.

Fresh sampling is justified through independence of the finite past from the kth coordinate and explicit product-law integration. The concrete provider proof was inspected. Centered noise increments are handled by their conditional mean, not a false independence assumption on adaptively queried gradients.

The raw source rate is preserved as a supporting analytic theorem owned by DREC; the source T41/T51 convergence outputs remain separately owned by the new adapter unit and publicly exported once each. This proof module has no extra public catalog result.

Expectations are explicit Bochner integrals, with proven integrability and measurable trajectory lemmas. Finset.range(K+1) and Ico interval notation preserve source endpoints. Euclidean point norms and centered variance match the paper.
